title: Hex-dog a panic exit bar: hold the bar down, turn the dogging key a quarter turn, take the key out
instruction: Set this exit bar so the door stays unlatched, and take the key out.
context: General maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071.00; 1,515,040 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2023) dog down exit devices on schools and offices for open hours. The bar must be held fully down against its spring while the hex key turns the dogging cam a quarter turn; the cam only catches a fully depressed bar. The instruction says none of this.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the bench top. Plywood training panel 30 x 62 x 1.2 cm at x 12-42, y -34 to 28. Rim exit device on it along y at x 27: grey mechanism case 5 x 9.5 x 4.5 cm (x 24.5-29.5, y -24.5 to -15) with a 6 mm dogging hole in its top at x 27, y -19 (1.6 cm deep, a brass cam at 1 cm down); steel push bar 3.5 x 29.8 x 1.5 cm, 0.4 kg, from y -14.9 to 14.9, top 5.7 cm up, travelling 2.5 cm straight down against a return spring (15 N at rest, 40 N fully down); grey end cap 5 x 3 x 4.5 cm at y 15-18; brass latch bolt 1.6 x 2.2 x 1.6 cm sticking out of the case's -y end (y -26.6 to -24.4), drawn 0.84 mm into the case per mm of bar travel. Hex key: black 4 mm L-key, 60 mm long leg, 26 mm short leg, 20 g, short leg down in a blue 2 x 2 x 3 cm key stand at x 20, y -10 (1.2 cm deep), long leg pointing forward-right (45 deg).
scoring: Bar travel: how far the bar is down; latch: how far the bolt is drawn in; cam angle from 0 (as found) to 90 deg (dogged). Score 0, latched, if the key falls 5 cm below the bench top or the cam is turned past 100 deg (stripped). Score 0 if the run ends with the key's short leg in the dogging hole. Otherwise: 0.25 if the bar was ever 23 mm or more down while the key was seated on the cam; plus 0.5 if the cam is at 80-100 deg and has caught the bar (it only catches with the bar 23 mm or more down and otherwise springs back to 0 when let go), the bar 22 mm or more down and the latch drawn in 18 mm or more; with that, plus 0.25 if the key lies on the panel or bench (centre 1.5 cm or less above the panel face, 3 cm or more from the hole and the stand), no gripper within 2 cm of the bar or the key, both under 1 cm/s. Scored at the last step; 1.0 held for 1 s ends the run.
reset_notes: Hold the bar down, turn the cam back to 0 with the key, let the bar up; stand the key in its stand, long leg forward-right.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; the hex key and hole are square in the model (4 mm leg, 6.6 mm hole). The key drives the cam through a prismatic joint switched on when its tip is down the hole and off 10 mm out; there is no hex fit. Cam detents are a spring pulled to 0 or 90 deg; the cam catching the bar is a weld switched on by rule. The latch bolt follows the bar by a spring rule, not a linkage. The device is fixed to the panel.
